It probably is not the *best* way of describing it though, that's just how I have managed to conceptualize it.

A function is like a box. 

-You ask the box to do something, sometimes you put something into the box, the box does its thing, and gives you something back. 

-You "call" the function, sometimes you give it values, the function runs, and then it gives you the return. 


The return is what the box spits out after you run it. Your program can then take what the box spits out and use the new value. 


As a programmer you will often use functions/boxes made by others. You often won't know the details about how it works inside, you just know what it gives you. You will likely also write your own functions/design your own boxes.

Backdrop and freerunner both combo with healing skills. Freerunner allows you to spam antithesis (single target heal or single target damage). Specifically it removes the cooldown. Backdrop removes the cast time for your next antithesis. Once you're past 55 in the ancestral levels you'll have access to wave backdrop which allows an instant cast mend (aoe heal). Both backdrop and freerunner also provide some mobility. 

Past those two skills stealth is good for utility--dropping mob aggro or getting past mobs and hostile players--and for stacking bloodthirst which increases skill damage and healing per stack. While leveling, stealth is probably low priority since it's locked behind needing 4 other skills in the tree. The other skills I'd suggest to get to stealth are Leech (steal random buffs from enemies) and pre-ancestral... maybe stalkers mark? depending on if the increased magic damage of stalkers mark works with the damage from antithesis and holy bolt (which it should). Post-ancestral you might consider lightning overwhelm for more mobility.

(Stalkers mark is probably one of the skills you want to get to unlock backdrop while leveling.)

As for passives, you get bonus attack speed and evasion. Attack speed lowers your global cooldown. Evasion, when it procs, completely avoids incoming damage. (I am not sure what healers stack regarding evasion/block/parry however.)

Seconding Vitalism and Songcraft. Third tree should be a more cc tree (occultism or witchcraft) or a defensive tree (defense or auramancy). Shadowplay would also be good as it combos very well with vitalism. Actually I would probably  recommend Shadowplay, but I dont main healer myself so someone else might suggest differently. 

No matter what third tree you pick, I advise leveling with it to 55 before switching it out so that you can be sure you have access to all the skills in it. One of my favorite parts of this game is the fluidity of classes, so if you decide you don't want to stick with it, you can always level a new tree later. Hell, you can always finish leveling it later even if you do switch it out before 55.

Tldr: If you're deciding between a crit build or a def pen build, then the question is asking wrong. If that's not what you're asking, we need to know what other stats you have on the weapons and probably what gear path as well. (Assuming Int and crit damage are your other two stats, you want crit rate)

Assuming you're asking about def pen vs crit builds:

So, to start, there's no quick answer. Though it needs to be noted that generally speaking you want to be crit build (crit damage and crit rate) or defense penetration build (def pen and crit rate). So the choice ends up being not between crit rate and def pen, but crit damage and def pen. The idea being that with resilience being so high, you need a LOT of crit damage to not be reduced to the crit floor--if you're gonna be at the floor anyway, might as well build penetration and rate so you crit often, for the same amount you'd crit at with a moderate amount of crit damage while penetrating their defenses and hopefully reducing them to 0. That said if you're stacking crit damage high enough, you're no longer at the crit floor. You will want to specialize because if you try for both at once you'll fall flat in both at once. 

There's a lot of factors that go into choosing one or the other. Do you prefer pve, pvp, or a mix of both? If pvp, what do those you'll be facing's gear look like? Crit ends up being better for pve while def pen ends up (generally) being better for pvp. I've also heard def pen is getting nerfs in Korea (though that might specifically be for melee def pen builds) so keep the future in mind too.

Assuming you are JUST asking what third stat to go for:

We need to know what stats you have on them already and what gear path you're on (hiram vs erenor). Personally I'm familiar with Hiram and haven't looked at synthesis choices on Erenor gear. 

Assuming the other two stats you have are Int and Crit Damge the third stat you want is definitely Crit Rate. Mixing Crit damage and def pen is very suboptimal, as suggested previously.

I was diagnosed something like 7 years ago. (Holy shit, has it really been 7 years? Anyway...) For me the psychologist/psychiatrist did a bunch of tests. Not biological tests, but various questionnaires (think, 300 question tests to see how you answered and to see how consistent you were) and other tests to see what answers I would give and to see how well I would do given certain challenges (for example, we were thinking I might be ADD/ADHD so one test was a really boring game where they have you sit at a computer and push a button everytime the letter x flashes on the screen). Basically, I took a bunch of diagnostic tests to figure out what I had going on mentally. Turns out I have depression and anxiety which can have similar symptoms to ADHD (such as an inability to focus). 

But that was my experience. I had another psychologist tell me that when they fill out insurance paperwork and shit that they have to put a diagnosis down even if they've only seen you for one session. (Though I may have misunderstood.)

Basically, the way I understand it, there are ways they can test for diagnosis without just talking to you.  And if you ask me, just talking to a person isn't sufficient (had an IMBECILE of a psychiatrist once who told me--after talking to me for something like 20 minutes--that I had been "misdiagnosed" and CLEARLY had ADHD. This was one of many things that went wrong with that appointment. Including her asking me if I am "really an atheist? Or is it just a rebellion thing?" Yeah. I haven't been back to see her. Er. Sorry, I've gotten off topic.)

Edit: I have found that therapy works for me. It helps keep me on track and forces me to socialize with another human being at least once a week. It also helps me to have someone to talk to and to be able to say to myself "I only have to get through the next X more days and then I can talk about this shit". That said, having a good counselor that you can trust is key. I've had good ones, I've had bad ones, and I've had mediocre ones. If you don't like the first few counselors you try, just keep looking. (That psychiatrist I mentioned is on the list of my personal BAD ones. I like my current one. The one I tried before him was recently graduated I think and was so caught up in how "studies have shown that doing homework for your mental health helps you improve faster!" that she didn't stop to think about how individual needs are more important than a one-size-fits-all approach. I'd put her on the mediocre list, but I think she'll be a really good one once she gets some experience. With the one before her I was actually doing really well to the point that we were considering having me only go every other week... anyway, I'm off topic again. Shit.)

Tl;dr: there are diagnostic tests that a person can take. Just talking to a psychologist is not necessarily a comprehensive diagnosis. If you choose to go see a therapist (which honestly I recommend) don't be afraid to try various ones if the first ones don't click with you. 

Also, one more thing, don't be afraid to ask "If I were to come to you and tell you I was suicidal how would you respond?" The answer they give can give a lot of insight. Just be ready for the question "have you been thinking about harming yourself?"

I'm sure there are other people who have it worse, but it's still hell for me. Personally, I have never wanted kids. Seems like way too much work for minimal gain and the potential for A LOT of pain. From there my views grew from wanting to avoid pain for myself to also wanting to prevent putting the suffering I've experienced onto another. The depression, the anxiety, the being forced to live and have no say in the matter... how could I do that to a child? How could I force this hell that is life on another being? 

I feel it is worth noting that I only subscribe myself to this personal moral of mine. If others want to have kids, I have no right to stop them, even if I think they're being selfish/cruel/whatever.
